quest.title: A Prophecy From the Past
quest.description: The story in the book seems to describe Durin's experiences. Curious about what remains untold, you and Durin step back into its pages to uncover the missing parts of his story.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x350, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Durin! Any more clues for us? We're all set for the next chapter!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's do this!

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Yeah, I was just about to come find you... Let's see what it says.

dialogues.speaker: Unknown Voice
dialogues.text: Now sprout to life the story's seeds, stirred by windborne melodies.

dialogues.speaker: Unknown Voice
dialogues.text: Then on that breeze the music leaves, fading into distant memories.

dialogues.speaker: Unknown Voice
dialogues.text: Seek the place where wind and tale entwine, and once there, make three riddles into verse, and three melodies into song.

dialogues.speaker: Unknown Voice
dialogues.text: For in poetry and song will this story start to blossom.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Uh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: C'mon, another riddle? All that talk about wind and melodies... Ugh, what do you think the answer could be?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wind, melodies, Mondstadt... Are you thinking what I'm thinking?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh... Ohhhh!

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: ...Care to elaborate?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wind, music, poetry... Tone-Deaf Bard's gotta know the answer!

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: You mean... Lord Barbatos?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You know too!?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Albedo introduced us when I first arrived in Mondstadt. I mean, someone like me was bound to catch his eye sooner or later.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's better that it's out in the open, anyway! Now, how should we track him down?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I'm pretty sure he's already "caught wind" of what's going on here. Why don't we just... see where the wind takes us?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, right! He definitely makes it easy to forget he's a real god sometimes...

talks.objective: Follow the guidance to find Venti

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon... What a sight for sore eyes! Ah, and the little dragon from the fairytale world!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: I heard your voices calling out to me on the wind. Something about... needing help with a riddle?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Sorry to disturb you, Lord Barbatos...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Hah, disturb me? Not at all! To tell you the truth, I'm just as curious about this riddle as you are. Let me take a look.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Hmm... Haha...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What is it? Did you figure out the answer?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Three riddles and three melodies... Hehe, that sure takes me back. The answer you seek lies hidden in memory.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like running to Tone-Deaf Bard was the right call, after all!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Long ago, those mages came to Mondstadt, seeking to test their strength against mine.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: But I replied, "Let us make music, not war, and resolve our conflicts through song."

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: So I strummed my lyre and sang them this verse:

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: "O wind, O wind, welcome now my guests."

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: "Pass through verdant leaves unseen, where shape your formless self may take, and offer up a graceful scene, a fleeting gift for welcome's sake."

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: "Leap at the edge of a sea of clouds, where land meets sky, and sky meets ground, there frighten off the noisy crowds, and bring my guests a calm profound."

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: "Fly beneath the stars up high, where mortal noise is swept aside, that my dear guests, with starry eyes, may share the dreams they hold inside."

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: "Now go to where I vowed to keep, a quiet spot for them to sleep."

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: "No clash, no contest bars the way, just tea and mirth to fill the day."

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: There you have it — the three melodies. As for the answers to those three riddles, I trust you can guess them by now?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: The woods, the edge of a cliff, and... the sky?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Correct! Funnily enough, your mother was also the first to solve it, all that time ago.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Heh, there must be some kind of special rapport between those who write stories and those who sing them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The woods, a cliff, and the sky... Ohhhh, so that's where it is!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: I suppose the spot that answer points to is where you're headed next.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: You should know, after solving my riddle, the mages even accepted my proposal, and made that location their official meeting spot.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: And going by what your book is suggesting, once you've found it, you might wanna try playing the melody I just shared with you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Guess you can be pretty reliable when it counts, huh, great Anemo Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Thanks for the help, Lord Barbatos. Um...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Still got questions for me, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Yeah, um... You must have read countless tales in your time, being a wandering bard and all. In your experience, why might an author consider a story "unfinished"?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Unfinished? Hm, well, I guess if there's something left to accomplish in the story, or um... Oh! If the last line goes: "To be continued..."

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: ...Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, your helpfulness lasted for, like, one second...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: In all seriousness, I would think, the answer to that question lies in your mother's story itself. It's not my place to pry any further.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Hm... Alright then, we should get going.

talks.objective: Head to the mages' meeting spot

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, we're here! Now, we just need to play the three melodies, and we should be able to gather the memories for the next chapter, right?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: A musical performance, huh... Out of all the things Miss Lisa has taught me, that's the one I'm worst at...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Leave it to me.

talks.objective: Enter the world within the book

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: I wonder when their next meeting will be...

talks.objective: Learn the story from the narrator

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, we're back in the story world, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: As if from nowhere, new guests appeared at the witches' table. Perhaps they too had come to celebrate the dragon-child's birthday.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Yet while everyone else was busy thinking about what kind of gift to offer, these three seemed to have come... empty-handed.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: ...Hardly the recipe for a warm welcome to a birthday party, now is it?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: A gift?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, what's this all about? We only just found out this was a party!

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: While the guests voiced their complaints and grievances, perhaps they should have been wondering what kind of gift to give instead...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, we need to bring a gift to advance the story... But where are we supposed to get something like that!?

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Perhaps it would be a good idea to... have a look around.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why didn't you just say so!?

dialogues.speaker: Observe
dialogues.text: (A toy sword. Perfect for a little warrior in the making.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, could we use these as gifts, maybe?

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: At last, the guests found something to give the dragon child.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Guess that's a yes, then... Hmm, which one should we go for?

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Still, the guests wondered, what kind of gift might the little dragon really want?

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Should they put a warrior's sword in his hand and send him out on an unstoppable quest to save the world?

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Or perhaps a wandering hero's slingshot, and the promise of a life of endless, uncharted adventure?

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Or maybe even a scholar's tome and the chance to take on all the world's unsolved mysteries?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, wow, that's a lot of pressure all of a sudden...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What do you think, Durin?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh yeah! Technically, we're actually picking a gift for you! So... which one would you prefer?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: You want... me to choose? Wow, this feels... kinda special.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How come?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: For as long as I can remember, I've spent most of my time living in the stories my mother created.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I always thought my mother had everything written out for me already — just like the toy figures in Constellation Metropole. What I wanted to do with my own future... Huh, that's something I've never really thought about.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: What did I want back then...? Ah... This is the first time I've ever asked myself that question.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like this is the perfect opportunity to answer it, then!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's been a while since you left Simulanka. And, after everything that's happened, it might be about time to start thinking about your future.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Hm... Then let me give it some thought.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's go with this one.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: In the end, the guests settled on... the warrior's sword.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So your dream is to become a warrior?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I just... really want to be able to keep people safe.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: If my time in Nod-Krai taught me anything, it's that a lot of problems in this world can only be settled by strength of arms.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: As long as I can help people, that's enough for me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're doing a great job already.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Really? But... I don't think it's enough...

talks.objective: Attend the birthday celebration with the gift

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, they should let us in now that we've got a gift, right?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Hello there. Brought a gift this time.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: The newly arrived guest presented his gift, wishing the little dragon a future as an indomitable warrior.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: The newly arrived guest presented his gift, wishing the little dragon a future as a wandering hero, free and unburdened.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: The newly arrived guest presented his gift, wishing the little dragon a future as a wise and accomplished scholar.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Accepting the guest's blessing, the story-witch invited him and his friends to take their place around the table.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Finally, she could introduce them all to her dragon-child, telling all in attendance about the moment of his hatching, and of course, the name he'd been given...

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: It was then that the seer-witch, diviner of the stars, withdrew her gaze from the heavens and turned a sorrowful glance upon the little dragon.

dialogues.speaker: Seer-Witch
dialogues.text: You gave him the same name as that evil dragon?

dialogues.speaker: Story-Witch
dialogues.text: That's right. But the life I intend for him shall be very different.

dialogues.speaker: Seer-Witch
dialogues.text: What folly, to love so blindly — for as you must know, a name is the mirror of destiny itself. He who bears an evil dragon's name must also inherit the fate of its previous owner.

dialogues.speaker: Seer-Witch
dialogues.text: His fate... has been foretold.

dialogues.speaker: Story-Witch
dialogues.text: ...Then I'll rewrite it.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: The witches at the table fell silent, for they knew the seer-witch's words had never once proven wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Yet just as clearly, they recognized the story-witch's resolve, for there is scarce a force in this world more fearsome than a mother's love.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: At last, the merry-witch stepped forward, dispelling the uneasy silence.

dialogues.speaker: Merry-Witch
dialogues.text: So be it — then we'll all lend a hand. Together, we shall rewrite this child's fate!

dialogues.speaker: Seer-Witch
dialogues.text: You mean to defy one of the fundamental rules of this world?

dialogues.speaker: Merry-Witch
dialogues.text: I refuse to be shackled by such "rules." Besides, this is a witches' gathering, is it not? What could be more fitting a subject for this occasion than to defy them?

dialogues.speaker: Sage-Witch
dialogues.text: Oh? Sounds like an interesting experiment...

dialogues.speaker: Seer-Witch
dialogues.text: I suppose, were we to succeed in this endeavor, we might bring a touch of wonder to this otherwise dreary sky of stars...

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: The merry-witch finally talked them all round, just like she had done many times before.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Warm and strong as the sun she was — so much so, in fact, that those who her light shined down upon had no choice but to bask in it.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: And so the witches readied their gifts, three marvels of the cosmos.

dialogues.speaker: Seer-Witch
dialogues.text: For this child, I shall decipher the ravings of the heavens and lay bare before him the trickery of fate.

dialogues.speaker: Sage-Witch
dialogues.text: For this child, I shall leave a formula powerful enough to unravel the very origins of this world, that he may seek another solution for the conundrum of his life.

dialogues.speaker: Merry-Witch
dialogues.text: For this child, I shall call upon wondrous magic to make possible his impossible wish.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: All the story-witch had was the pen in her hand, yet with the love that flowed from it, she resolved to bring forth a marvel of her own.

dialogues.speaker: Story-Witch
dialogues.text: For this child, I shall leave behind the last story I will ever write, and with it, a path to an ending yet untold.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: With the witches' blessings given and received, the little dragon's fate at last began to turn.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep... Looks like we've completed this chapter, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Those witches in the story were the mages of the Hexenzirkel, right? They sure seemed to care a lot about you, Durin!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, uh... Paimon kinda had trouble following their conversation. Just a bunch of mystery, as usual...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: The evil dragon's fate...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohhh, is that what you're worried about? But... didn't we already take care of that?

choices.text: Yeah, after what happened in Simulanka...

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Ahh... The mages must have had a hand in that too.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Also, I was just thinking... Which part of the story are we even meant to be "completing"?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It feels less like we're filling in the gaps, and more like we're adding something new altogether...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But, we used the ink, right? And the book hasn't given us any more clues, so that must mean our task is complete — at least for now.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Yeah, I guess we're doing something right...

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Hm... Maybe I'm overthinking things. It's just, this is my mother's final wish, so I don't want to mess it up.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Anyway, thanks for all your help. I'll let you know as soon as the book reveals a hint about the next chapter.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay then! See you in the next chapter!

choices.text: Even if we run into trouble, we can always go ask Alice.

talks.objective: Discuss your experience within the story with Durin

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Wait, this pen...

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: What the guests saw before them was none other than the witch's pen, the source of countless moving tales.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So this is M's pen? The one she used to write the story of Simulanka? You must know it well, Durin...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Honestly, the thing I remember most is how often I woke up to the sound of it scribbling away...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: In the years before my mother passed away, she'd often sit at her desk writing late into the night. Almost like... like she was in a race against time to get something completed.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sounds like a tough line of work...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Anyway, it belonged to my mother, so we shouldn't mess with it. Let's go see what else there is.

dialogues.speaker: Observe
dialogues.text: (A little slingshot. Just the thing for a wandering hero-to-be.)

dialogues.speaker: Observe
dialogues.text: (A tome. The ideal gift for a budding scholar.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's go with this one.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: In the end, the guests settled on... the wandering hero's slingshot.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A wandering hero... So you're an explorer, just like us!

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I guess you inspired me, hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: During our journey from Mondstadt to Nod-Krai, we passed through many places and encountered all sorts of different people.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: But despite the immense distances between them, there was always one topic that kept cropping up — your accomplishments.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe... Well, we are world-renowned adventurers, after all!

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Come to think of it... Isn't a wandering hero basically the same thing as an adventurer?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I've always thought of adventurers as people who chase after stories, and in doing so, they also leave behind many of their own.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I'd like to become someone like that too.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's go with this one.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: In the end, the guests settled on... the scholar's tome.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you're the scholarly type, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I just feel like... I should learn more about the way the world works.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What makes you say that?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Um... I'll give you an example. Did you know that in Mondstadt, using fire to catch fish is a punishable offense?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm guessing... Klee took you fish blasting?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I thought she was just teaching me regular hunting techniques. It was only after Master Jean caught me and sent me to solitary confinement that I realized I'd misread the situation...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: So much of what's considered common knowledge in your world just wasn't in Simulanka. So, I have to learn, or I'll keep causing trouble for everyone else.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Paimon's not sure that counts as "common" knowledge...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, is that... the other Durin?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's the storybook Durin.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Mini Durin!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nope, no reaction... Seriously, did he doze off at his own birthday party!?

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Brought to life by the witch's magic ink, the dragon-child played with animated glee each time the tip of her pen danced across the page.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Yet she could not spend all her time writing. For the upcoming witches' gathering, she had no choice but to set down her pen.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: But before doing so, she wrote one last line: "So did the child drift off into blissful slumber."

choices.text: So, the reason she never wrote the little dragon's reaction...

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Strange, I don't remember ever being at any of the mages' gatherings. When exactly was this birthday party supposed to have happened...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No wonder you don't remember — from the looks of it, you were probably fast asleep at the time!

choices.text: ...Was because she ran out of time?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's keep looking.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: The witches went on chatting away, ignoring the empty-handed guests.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: The guests hesitated, and not without good reason. Given how much this gift would mean to the little dragon, a bit of careful thought could go a long way...

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: No mark had been left on the page ahead. The group found themselves unable to move forward...

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: For in poetry and song will this story start to blossom.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: The witches readied their gifts, three marvels of the cosmos.
